beats: Hook: QC01-03 said noise killed analog computers (reuse line_qc_analog_machine_room, line_qc_analog_two_dials). A qubit is analog too: its errors are tiny over-rotations, not clean flips (line_qc_digital_tiny_nudge: the lever leans, it is not flipped). So why can a code that only knows "flip" and "sign" fix all of them? Cast as in QC08-01: the keeper (the code) and the imp (the noise); this part is cut from the start of Q25-11, which finishes Q25-10's story, so it keeps that lecture's cast. The imp's square glasses are the sign trick, as in QC08-03.

R = m I + n X on the repetition code (Q25-11 10:02-14:45; Q24-09 68:32-72:58; tape Q24-09 p24): the nudged state is a blend of "nothing happened" and "switch 1 flipped"; the syndrome measurement makes it choose, no error with odds |m|^2 or a whole X with odds |n|^2 (line_qc_digital_spinner_two: one big section, one thin slice), and each outcome is one the code already fixes (line_qc_digital_snap_two_ways). Honest caveat in the narration: the spinner shows only the odds of the check's answer; the lean is not a hidden flip waiting to be found.

The analog callback (Q25-11 15:12-16:37, clip "measurement-induced collapse is a saver for quantum computing"; Q24-09 75:53-76:44, clip "unlike analog computing, you can correct it because you do a collapse"): a nudged dial never snaps back (reuse line_qc_analog_two_dials, line_qc_analog_two_valleys); the check turns a small drift into a rare, whole, fixable flip.

Linearity (Q25-11 16:47-19:23; Q24-09 73:28-75:27; tape Q24-09 p26): correct A and B and you correct any combination of them; I, X, Y, Z span all 2x2 matrices, and Y ~ XZ is flip and sign at once (line_qc_digital_four_moves: do nothing, flip, the square-glasses trick, both; line_qc_digital_spinner_four: the check picks one of the four; reuse line_qc_undo_two_prisms, QC05-01: split, treat each part, recombine, captioned as a picture of the recipe, not of physics).

Small errors on every qubit (Q24-11 04:47-06:45; tape Q24-11 s4): expand the product; the one-qubit terms are first order, the two-qubit terms second order (epsilon^2), so the case the code cannot fix is rare (line_qc_digital_feather_row).
Takeaway: computes like analog, corrects like digital, because looking forces the choice; pays off QC01-03. Check the discretization of errors against Nielsen and Chuang, section 10.2.
Cover (line_qc_cover_08_04; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the imp nudges a lever a hair; the keeper spins a spinner with one big section and one thin slice.
